1.title: Build Reports: Visuals, Formatting, Filtering and Pages
1.text: Welcome to Module nine: Build Reports: Visuals, Formatting, Filtering and Pages. It covers the exam area Visualize and analyze the data. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do seven things. Select an appropriate visual. Format and configure visuals. Apply and customize a theme. Apply conditional formatting. Apply slicing and filtering. Configure the report page. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Visualize and analyze the data (twenty-five-thirty percent). Exam format: a one hundred-minute proctored exam; a score of seven hundred on a scale to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official P L three hundred study guide, skills measured as of April twenty, twenty twenty-six.

1.title: Choose the right visual
1.text: Choose the right visual. Match the question the viewer asks to the visual that answers it best.

1.title: Choose the right visual, continued
1.text: Choose the right visual. The figure shows this: Chooser that matches each viewer question, such as comparison, trend, part-to-whole, relationship, single number, geography, detail and flow, to the best Power B I visual.

1.title: Choose the right visual, continued
1.text: Choose the right visual. Comparison between categories. Clustered bar or column chart. Trend over time. Line chart or area chart. Part-to-whole, few parts. Stacked column, donut or pie chart. Part-to-whole, many parts. Treemap. Relationship of two measures. Scatter chart (bubble size adds a third). Single number. Card; K P I for value against target; gauge for progress to a goal. Geography. Map, filled map or shape map. Detail rows. Table, or matrix for row and column groups. Flow and variance. Waterfall chart or funnel chart.

1.title: Choose the right visual, continued
1.text: Choose the right visual. A waterfall shows a start value rising and falling to an end value. A funnel shows stages that shrink, such as leads to orders. A matrix adds row and column groups with drill and expand; a table is a flat list. Exam tip: Waterfall means variance to a total, funnel means shrinking stages, scatter means relationship, K P I means value against a target. Use pie or donut only for a few parts and a treemap for many.

1.title: Format visuals and apply a theme
1.text: Format visuals and apply a theme. Fields decide what a visual shows. Format decides how it looks. On the Visualizations pane, the Build visual tab holds the field wells, such as Axis, Legend and Values. The Format visual tab holds appearance. Changing Sum to Average is a field change, not a format change.

1.title: Format visuals and apply a theme, continued
1.text: Format visuals and apply a theme. Title. Where: General tab. What it controls: Text, font and alignment of the title. Axes. Where: Visual tab. What it controls: Show or hide, range, display units, axis title. Data labels. Where: Visual tab. What it controls: Values on the marks, units, decimals. Legend. Where: Visual tab. What it controls: Series names, position, or off. Colors. Where: Visual tab. What it controls: Data color per series or category. A theme is a Jason file that sets colors, fonts and default visual formatting for the whole report. Applying a theme removes report-level customizations you made earlier.

1.title: Format visuals and apply a theme, continued
1.text: Format visuals and apply a theme. Apply. Pick a built-in theme in the Themes gallery on the Design tab. Customize. Choose Customize theme to edit colors, text and visual defaults. Import and export. Load a theme from a Jason file; Save current theme writes one. Accessible. Color-blind friendly and high contrast themes sit in the gallery. Exam tip: A theme is a Jason file: Customize theme edits it, Save current theme exports it, Import loads it. To meet an accessibility need, start from an accessible theme in the gallery.

1.title: Conditional formatting
1.text: Conditional formatting. Conditional formatting changes a color, bar or icon based on the data. It works on the values of tables and matrices (not on headers). It also works on column and bar charts, cards and button slicers. The types are Background color, Font color, Data bars, Icons and Web U R L.

1.title: Conditional formatting, continued
1.text: Conditional formatting. Gradient. A color scale between a low and a high color, with an optional middle color. Rules. If-then conditions on value ranges, one color per rule. Field value. A field or measure returns the color: a C S S name, hex code, R G B value, or the theme names good, bad and neutral.

1.title: Conditional formatting, continued
1.text: Conditional formatting. Three rules to remember. A text value cannot be colored directly: write a measure that returns the color and use Field value. For percent fields, enter rule values as decimals, such as zero point one, with the type Number. Conditional formatting overrides custom colors set by hand. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study. Exam tip: Three format styles: Gradient, Rules, Field value. If a measure returns the color, the answer is Field value. If you need a color for text, you need a measure.

1.title: Slicing and filtering
1.text: Slicing and filtering. A slicer is a visual on the canvas. A filter lives in the Filters pane. Both narrow the data, but viewers use them differently. List or tile. Picking one or many categories. Dropdown. Long lists in little space. Between, before, after. Numeric or date ranges. Relative date. Rolling periods such as the last thirty days. Hierarchy. Several fields in one slicer, such as Category then Product.

1.title: Slicing and filtering, continued
1.text: Slicing and filtering. The Filters pane has three levels. Filters on this visual affect one visual. Filters on this page affect every visual on the page. Filters on all pages are report-level and affect every page. The filter types are Basic (tick values), Advanced (conditions such as contains or greater than), Top N and Relative date. A Top N filter keeps the top or bottom number of items by a measure, such as the top five products by sales. It stays correct as data changes. A relative date filter keeps a window that moves with today's date, such as the last three calendar months.

1.title: Slicing and filtering, continued
1.text: Slicing and filtering. Where. Slicer: On the canvas, visible. Filter in the Filters pane: In the Filters pane. Scope. Slicer: Its page, or more pages with sync. Filter in the Filters pane: Visual, page or report. Viewer. Slicer: Clicks it as a control. Filter in the Filters pane: Can change it unless the author locks or hides it. A slicer filters every visual on its page unless Edit interactions says otherwise (Module eleven). Exam tip: Filter levels are visual, page and all pages. Choose a slicer when viewers must see and change the selection on the page, and a filter when the author sets the scope.

2.title: The report page and paginated reports
2.text: The report page and paginated reports. Page settings sit in the Format page pane and the View tab. Page size. sixteen:nine, four:three, Letter, Tooltip or Custom. Canvas background. Color or image of the page itself. Wallpaper. The area behind the page canvas. Alignment. Vertical position of the canvas in the window. Page information. Page name, Allow use as tooltip, and Q and A use of the page. Page view. Fit to page, Fit to width or Actual size.

2.title: The report page and paginated reports, continued
2.text: The report page and paginated reports. Page view only changes how you see the page. It does not change the page size. A paginated report is built for pixel-perfect layout, printing and sharing, and it shows all rows across as many pages as needed. You author it in Power B I Report Builder (free) and save it as an.rdl file. An interactive Power B I report is a.pbix file built for exploration.

2.title: The report page and paginated reports, continued
2.text: The report page and paginated reports. Invoices, statements, labels, or every row over many pages. Paginated report. Export to P D F, Word, Power Point, Excel, C S V, X M L or M H T M L. Paginated report. Slicers, cross-filtering, drillthrough, exploration. Power B I report. Viewers on a free license need the paginated report in a workspace on an F sixty-four or P one capacity. Exam tip: Printing, pixel-perfect or all rows across pages means a paginated report in Report Builder (.rdl). Interactive exploration means a Power B I report. Canvas background is the page; wallpaper is behind it.

2.title: Practice Question 1
2.text: Question one. A finance team needs a visual that shows how an opening balance rises and falls through several expense categories to reach a closing balance. Which visual fits best? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: A waterfall chart. A waterfall chart shows increases and decreases that lead to a total, which the other charts do not.

2.title: Practice Question 2
2.text: Question two. A table shows a text column Status. A measure returns a hex color code for every row, and the author wants each Status cell shaded with that color. Which format style should the author use? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Field value, based on the color measure. Field value applies colors that a field or measure returns, which is the only way to color text from a calculation.

2.title: Practice Question 3
2.text: Question three. Viewers must pick a product category directly on the report page and see the current selection at a glance. What should the author add? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: A slicer visual on the report page canvas. A slicer is a visual on the canvas, while filters live in the Filters pane.

2.title: Practice Question 4
2.text: Question four. A bar chart must always show the five products with the highest sales, even as the numbers change. What should the author configure? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: A Top N filter on Product, by the sales measure. A Top N filter re-ranks by the measure whenever the data changes, while the others stay fixed.

2.title: Practice Question 5
2.text: Question five. An author wants a gray area around the report page, while the page itself stays white. Which setting should the author change? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: The wallpaper setting in the Format page pane. Wallpaper colors the area behind the canvas, while canvas background colors the page itself.

2.title: Practice Question 6
2.text: Question six. A retailer needs invoices that print the same way every time, with all line items flowing across as many pages as needed. Which report type fits best? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: A paginated report built in Report Builder. Paginated reports are pixel-perfect for printing and show all rows across pages, unlike interactive reports and dashboards.

2.title: Recall Check 1
2.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What file format does a Power B I theme use? Answer: Jason. Question two. What are the three conditional formatting styles? Answer: Gradient, Rules and Field value. Question three. Which Filters pane level affects every page? Answer: Filters on all pages (report level).

2.title: Recall Check 2
2.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What are the three Page view options? Answer: Fit to page, Fit to width and Actual size. Question five. Which filter keeps a rolling window such as the last thirty days? Answer: A relative date filter. Question six. Which free tool authors paginated reports, and what is the file type? Answer: Power B I Report Builder, and an.rdl file.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. Visual choice: Compare: bar; trend: line; relationship: scatter; one number: card or K P I; variance: waterfall. Format versus fields: Fields decide content; Format visual decides look. Theme: Jason file; Customize theme, Save current theme, import; accessible themes in the gallery. Conditional formatting: Gradient, Rules, Field value; text needs a measure; percent as decimals. Filter levels: Visual, page, all pages; Basic, Advanced, Top N, Relative date. Slicer versus filter: Slicer on the canvas; filter in the Filters pane. Page settings: Size, canvas background, wallpaper, Page information; Page view is zoom only. Paginated report: Pixel-perfect, printing, all rows; Report Builder;.rdl.
